c6_free_family.title: The long table
c6_free_family.text: Your cousin pushes the pie across the table and looks at his plate. “I should have said it differently, that day.” “Yes,” you say. Then you pass the bread, and that is how it is mended.

c6_free_quill.title: Quill counts
c6_free_quill.text: Quill counts every basket twice. “A tenth,” he says, and writes it with a small flourish. “The Lord will like the numbers. I like them better.” He looks at your fields as if they were a poem.

c6_free_greenstem.title: Two healers
c6_free_greenstem.text: Greenstem takes the chest in both arms. “Wren says I may carry it to the village myself.” Wren, behind him, folds her arms and does not say a word. Her eyes say a lot.

c6_free_miller.title: The sails turn
c6_free_miller.text: The miller pours your flour into his hopper. The sails creak, then turn, slowly, as they did before the fire. “Hear that?” he says. “That is Hazelwood having bread again.”

c6_free_lark.title: Nutmeg
c6_free_lark.text: Lark holds out the cake. The squirrel takes it with both hands. “Nutmeg,” Lark announces. “Obviously.” The squirrel does not look as if it has any other opinion. You laugh until the fence shakes.

c6_free_garden.title: For the night garden
c6_free_garden.text: You set the bowl down at the edge of the garden. You open your mouth. You close it again. Far off, very softly, a very small bell rings twice. You nod, and walk home in the dark, and you are not afraid.
